reason: I want to follow how the kidney filters blood and recovers useful substances, starting with the blood and filtering unit.
expectation: I expect the nephron to filter some fluid from the blood, though I am unsure exactly what the result will show.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters would advance the organ assembly, but I want to see filtering first.

effect: The filter leaves blood cells and most proteins in the vessels while water and small substances enter the tubule. I’ll follow what is recovered next.
reaction: The contrast between what passes through and what stays in the blood is clear.
reason: Selective transporters seem like the next step in returning useful substances to the blood.
expectation: I expect some useful dissolved substances to move from the tubule back into the blood, though I’m unsure which ones will be shown.

alternatives.reason: Adding the ureters would advance the organ assembly, but I want to follow the filtered sample first.

effect: The tubule returns glucose and other useful substances to the blood; I’ll follow the remaining fluid next.
reaction: Recovering almost all filtered glucose makes the filtering and recovery sequence clearer.
reason: The water-permeable tubule looks like the next stage in following what the kidney recovers.
expectation: I expect some water to move from the tubule back into the blood, leaving a more concentrated fluid.

alternatives.reason: The ureters are needed for the organ assembly, but I want to finish following the sample first.

effect: Water returns to the blood while wastes remain in the tubule. I’ll follow the remaining fluid into urinary drainage.
reaction: The sequence from filtering to recovering useful substances is straightforward so far.
reason: Urinary drainage should complete the path of the remaining fluid.
expectation: I expect the remaining fluid to become urine and pass toward the ureter and bladder.

alternatives.reason: The ureters also need connecting, but I want to finish following the sample first.

effect: The remaining fluid has reached the bladder as urine, completing the filtering and recovery goal. I’ll connect the urinary organs next.
reaction: The route is clear, though the final drainage step adds little explanation.
reason: The ureters connect the kidneys toward the bladder, so they seem a useful first fitting.
expectation: I expect the ureters to be attached to the kidney pair, leaving the bladder to connect.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also needs fitting, but I chose to follow the route from kidneys outward.

effect: The ureters are fitted, leaving the bladder to connect to complete the urinary route.
reaction: The explanation reinforces the route already shown by the urine sample.
reason: The bladder is the only offered combination and completes the organ assembly.
expectation: I expect the bladder to be fitted to the kidney pair, connecting it to the ureters.

effect: The bladder is fitted, completing the kidney pair’s listed slots. The remaining combination connects the urinary organs to the body.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward and added no further explanation.
reason: The only offered combination connects the assembled urinary organs to the body, advancing the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the kidneys and urinary organs to join the body and its circulation, completing the goal.

effect: The kidneys and urinary tract are now connected to the body and its circulation, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The final picture ties the organ assembly to the blood-filtering sequence, although its explanation is brief.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following filtration with nutrient recovery was the most worthwhile part. Seeing glucose return to the blood clarified why filtration alone is not the whole job.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bladder was straightforward but added no explanation, and the ureter fitting repeated a route already shown.

surprise.text: I found it useful that almost all filtered glucose is normally recovered in healthy kidneys.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the organ fittings felt predictable after the urine route had already been shown.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in another chapter if it developed another connection between systems. This chapter's filtering and recovery sequence was clear, but the later fittings felt repetitive.
